questions.text: What interests you about applying your computing science background to a Graduate AI Engineer role supporting practical systems for mineral exploration?
questions.rationale: This opening question fits the mixed format and explores motivation while connecting the candidate’s current degree to the role’s applied AI context.
questions.job_requirement_excerpt: Support applied AI and machine-learning systems for mineral exploration.

questions.text: In your AI Coursework Prototype, how did the tool-call agent decide which local course tool to select, and what would you consider when validating its recorded tool results before producing a response?
questions.rationale: This probes the candidate’s directly evidenced agent prototype while targeting the role’s need to develop, validate, and iterate on AI agents.
questions.job_requirement_excerpt: Develop and evaluate machine-learning models and AI agents;

questions.text: Suppose you were building a Python model using incomplete and noisy exploration data: how would you structure an experiment, choose an evaluation approach, and decide what to change after reviewing the results?
questions.rationale: This assesses student-appropriate reasoning about experimentation, validation, and iteration against the job’s real-world data and machine-learning responsibilities without claiming prior experience the candidate has not evidenced.
questions.job_requirement_excerpt: Work with senior AI researchers, data engineers, and geoscientists on practical systems using incomplete and noisy real-world data.

questions.text: What interests you about moving from your computing science studies and software engineering projects into an AI Engineer role focused on LLM-powered applications?

questions.text: Walk me through how your AI Coursework Prototype selects tools and records their results, and explain one design change you would make to improve the reliability or observability of that agent workflow.

questions.job_requirement_excerpt: design and optimise RAG pipelines and AI-agent workflows

questions.text: Suppose you had to extend the Team Course Planner into a knowledge system that answers questions about course information: how would you design a simple RAG pipeline, and how would you evaluate whether its retrieval and answers were working well?

questions.text: Tell me about a time during your Coursework Retrieval Assistant project when you found that an answer was uncertain or the retrieved evidence was not sufficient. What did you do, and what did you learn?

questions.text: Suppose you were comparing two machine-learning models for a mineral-exploration dataset with noisy labels and an uneven class distribution. How would you design the evaluation, choose useful metrics, and decide what to investigate or change next?

questions.text: How would you evaluate whether an LLM-powered retrieval system is performing well, using the uncertainty cases you documented and the precision-and-recall comparisons from your classification study?
